approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock Apple TV documentation groups JavaScript command behavior as a core part of building TV applications, so TV app guidance should treat commands as part of navigation, media, utility, and demo workflows.

notes: Read-only source inspection verified Rock TV app templates use rockCommand attributes for navigation, login/logout, and media playback commands with command-specific parameters.
This confirms the command surface exists in local TV app implementation examples; agents still need to verify the exact current TV app/page template being edited.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Helix Lava Forms address the mismatch between independent HTML forms and ASP.NET WebForms' single-page form model, which matters when validating or troubleshooting nested form behavior.

Rock REST API requests require authorization; supported approaches include an HTTP cookie tied to an existing Rock user session or an `Authorization-Token`, which must accompany subsequent API requests.

Rock's Obsidian documentation is primarily written for the core developer team, but some sections such as Grids are published for broader public reading and require judgment when translating them to plugin development.

Rock plugin and theme packaging guidance frames the Rock Shop as the distribution path for community extensions, so plugin work should include packaging, review, and uninstall behavior rather than only local code changes.

An Obsidian block combines a C# block, a TypeScript component, and block actions, so developer guidance should connect server logic, client UI, and action endpoints instead of treating a block as one file.
Rock Mobile compatibility is two-dimensional: documentation uses `M` tags for minimum Mobile Shell versions and `C` tags for minimum Rock Core versions, and a feature may require both.
Roku commands are executed by setting a rockCommand and command-specific parameters on supported controls, and multiple commands can be chained by separating command names with commas.

notes: Read-only source inspection verified rockCommand usage with command-specific parameters such as video URL, media element GUID, title, artwork, related entity, watch map, and resume behavior.
The local templates verify the command pattern, but the comma-chaining behavior remains source-documentation-backed rather than independently exercised in a running Roku client.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Helix is a Rock web-development surface that combines HTMX, Lava Applications, Lava Commands, and Control Shortcodes as an evolution of Lava-driven web development.
Helix Lava Endpoints are the application work units called from the client, so agents should inspect endpoint name, description, slug, behavior, and security before changing an application flow.

notes: Read-only SQL verified LavaEndpoint and LavaApplication tables, endpoint/list/detail/content block types, live endpoint rows, and endpoint metadata columns for name, description, slug, HTTP method, security mode, enabled Lava commands, cache/rate-limit settings, active state, and additional settings.
This verifies where agents should inspect endpoint work units before changing a Helix application flow; it does not prove a specific endpoint is correctly configured.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Helix applications require explicit security and data-integrity review because endpoint-backed application surfaces can expose data or perform work beyond static content rendering.

notes: Read-only SQL verified LavaApplication and LavaEndpoint are secured entity types and that the connected instance has Auth rows for both application and endpoint entities.

Source/view-model evidence confirms endpoint surfaces include security mode, enabled Lava commands, CSRF, and rate-limit settings, supporting explicit security and data-integrity review before endpoint-backed work is changed.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Moving a Rock Mobile app from shell V5 or earlier to V6 or later changes the framework from Xamarin Forms to .NET MAUI; much XAML remains similar, but documented breaking layout behavior must be tested and adapted.

The Lava Application Content block automatically registers HTMX, and its templates can call an application endpoint with `^/application-slug/endpoint-slug` instead of hard-coding the full `/api/v2/lava-app/1/...` route.
